title: Per-token SLI + Multi-region Failover Heatmap and Circuit-breaker Telemetry
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: We currently lack fine-grained visibility into token-level latency distributions, the interaction between circuit breakers and load-shedding, and per-region failover behavior. This makes it hard to distinguish regressions caused by model/kernel changes from infrastructure pressure (e.g., overloaded queueing, scheduling backpressure).

Goal: Instrument a set of golden signals and derived SLIs that capture per-token latency, request-level tail behavior, circuit-breaker trips, shed request counts, and multi-region failover rates. Build a Grafana dashboard (and a condensed console view) to enable on-call diagnosis and SLO compliance reporting. Provide a validation and rollout plan to add telemetry with minimal perf overhead.

Scope:
- Define and emit token-level latency histograms and derived P50/P90/P99 (per-route and per-model).
- Emit request-level metadata: tokens_requested, tokens_generated, model_variant, region_origin, region_served, route_id, priority_tier.
- Record circuit-breaker events: cb_state_change, cb_tripped_count, cb_recovery_latency_ms.
- Record load-shedding events: shed_count, shed_reason (queue_timeout | memory_pressure | concurrency_limit).
- Multi-region failover metrics: failover_attempts, failover_successes, failover_switch_latency_ms, serving_region_heatmap.
- Build dashboards and SLO reports: per-route per-model token-latency SLI, region-failover heatmap, circuit-breaker timeline, and an alerting rule set for operational thresholds.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Use client-side buckets for token latency (exposure via Prometheus histograms) rather than per-token logs to avoid high cardinality logs and cost. Histograms will be coarse (power-of-two buckets tuned to token-latency distribution) to balance precision and ingestion cost.
- Emit aggregate counters for shed_count and cb_tripped_count by reason and region to keep cardinality bounded.
- Include a sampling mechanism for full per-request traces (1/1000 by default) to troubleshoot complex issues without instrumenting all requests.
- Add route_id and model_variant as labels, but cap distinct values via a route registry to prevent unbounded cardinality.

Telemetry schema (metric names and labels):
- rwi_token_latency_bucket{le, route_id, model_variant, region_served}
- rwi_token_latency_sum{route_id, model_variant, region_served}
- rwi_token_latency_count{route_id, model_variant, region_served}
- rwi_tokens_requested_total{route_id, priority_tier, region_origin}
- rwi_tokens_generated_total{route_id, model_variant, region_served}
- rwi_cb_tripped_total{cb_name, reason, region_served}
- rwi_cb_state{cb_name, state, region_served} (gauge: 0/1)
- rwi_shed_total{reason, region_served}
- rwi_failover_attempts_total{from_region, to_region, route_id}
- rwi_failover_success_total{from_region, to_region, route_id}
- rwi_failover_latency_ms_bucket/sum/count{from_region, to_region}

SLI definitions (examples):
- Per-token latency SLI (route R): fraction of tokens whose service latency <= 25ms at P99 across trailing 28 days. Implement as derived metric from histogram: (count_le_25ms / total_count). SLO target: 99.5% tokens <= 25ms for hosted-tier routes.
- Request-level availability SLI: fraction of successful responses (2xx/stream-end) excluding intentionally shed requests and planned maintenance. SLO target: 99.95 monthly.
- Failover success SLI: fraction of failover attempts that completed within 500ms and returned to healthy region. Target: 98%.
- Circuit-breaker health: rolling 1h cb_tripped_rate < 0.1% of requests; alert if >0.5%.

Dashboard & alerting:
- Grafana dashboard panels:
  1) Token latency heatmap: x-axis token position (0..n), y-axis latency buckets, series per-region or per-model.
  2) Token latency P50/P90/P99 over time by route and model variant.
  3) Serving region heatmap: fraction of traffic served by region for each origin region (matrix).
  4) Circuit-breaker timeline: state changes and tripped_count overlays with request load.
  5) Load-shedding timeline: shed_count by reason and region.
  6) Failover scatter: attempts vs success vs latency.
- Alerts to create (initial):
  - token_p99_latency > 40ms sustained 10m for production routes (alert to SRE + owning team).
  - cb_tripped_rate > 0.5% in 5m (pager).
  - failover_success_rate < 90% in 30m (pager).
  - shed_count spike > 3x baseline in 5m (page + ticket).

Implementation plan:
1) Schema & telemetry primitives (Week 1): define histogram buckets and stable label set; update telemetry SDK to export rwi_token_latency_* and aggregate counters.
2) Minimal emitting in serving runtime (Week 2-3): add nonblocking histogram updates at token commit points, emit shed/cb counters on state transitions. Feature flagged behind telemetry.v2.
3) Validate cost/overhead (Week 3): run A/B on staging with sampling off; measure CPU/alloc impact. If >1% p99 CPU, widen bucket width and re-evaluate.
4) Dashboard buildout (Week 4): create Grafana dashboard and Console condensed panels; wire SLO queries.
5) Rollout & runbook (Week 5): enable telemetry.v2 for 10% traffic, monitor; publish runbook with SRE-run steps and mitigation playbooks for CB trips and load-shedding.
6) Full rollout & SLO adoption (Week 6): enable for all hosted traffic, add SLOs to on-call dashboard.

Acceptance criteria:
- Instrumentation emits metrics listed in telemetry schema for all instrumented routes in staging.
- Grafana dashboard exists with the six panels described and links to traces.
- Overhead: additional CPU <1.5% 95th and Prometheus cardinality increase <10% for metrics ingestion cost.
- Runbook published and reviewed by SRE and two product teams.
- SLO queries validated and scheduled reporting enabled.

Testing & validation notes:
- Synthetic test harness: create replay workload with token-length distribution representative of production and inject controlled failure modes (high concurrency, simulated GPU slowdowns) to ensure histograms reflect degradation.
- Canary: telemetry.v2 on 10% traffic for 72h; compare metrics against sampling baseline.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.com/display/RWI/Token+SLIs+and+Failover+Telemetry (draft)
- Grafana dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/SlI123/token-metrics-heatmap
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4728 (instrumentation SDK changes)
- Runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A-Telemetry-Runbook

Risks & mitigations:
- Cardinality explosion from route/model labels -> enforce route registry and sanitize model_variant labels; fallback to "unknown_variant" for >50 distinct variants.
- Performance overhead -> feature-flagged rollout and A/B tests; use coarse buckets when needed.
- Missed edge cases for failover labeling -> ensure failover path attaches from_region and to_region before metric emission.

Next steps (owner: Diego Ramos):
- Finalize histogram buckets and label whitelist by 2026-02-16.
- Create telemetry SDK PR and link.
- Draft Grafana dashboard and request SRE review.
